title: Magnetic Couplings in Half-Filled Bipartite Graphs
abstract: We break from perturbative frameworks to establish a non-perturbative generalization of magnetic exchange rules in half-filled bipartite networks. While historical models remain strictly tied to the debatable perturbation approach in the dilute limit and require the absence of zero-energy modes, our universal mechanism governs exchange interactions across arbitrary bipartite graphs. By bypassing traditional expansion bottlenecks, this framework provides an analytical predictive tool for magnetism in complex lattices, offering key design principles to engineer stable, long-range order in next-generation 2D spintronic devices
summary: This work develops a non-perturbative theory to calculate magnetic exchange couplings in half-filled bipartite magnetic lattices. By utilizing the Magnetic Force Theorem and circumventing issues related to zero-energy modes, the authors provide a universal analytical tool. This tool offers key design principles for engineering stable magnetic order in advanced 2D spintronic materials.
main_problem: To establish a non-perturbative generalization of magnetic exchange rules in half-filled bipartite networks, overcoming the limitations of traditional perturbative frameworks.
main_result: The derived non-perturbative formula for magnetic coupling is universal, valid for any bipartite graph, and successfully bypasses the problematic zero-energy mode (ZEM) calculations.
method: The magnetic coupling is calculated using the Magnetic Force Theorem (MFT) and Green's functions, leading to a generalized, non-perturbative expression involving frequency integrals.
model_or_system: The system is a magnetic bipartite graph (MBG) modeled by a Hamiltonian incorporating hopping terms ($t_{AB}$) and local Heisenberg exchange interactions ($J$). The analysis focuses on half-filled systems with localized magnetic moments on two sublattices (A and B).
key_observables: Magnetic couplings $J_{\lambda\lambda'}(R)$, generalized susceptibility $\chi_{\lambda\lambda'}^{ij}(\omega)$, and the existence/weight of Zero-Energy Modes (ZEMs).
important_parameters: Half-filling ($\Lambda$), the coupling strength $J_S$, and the lattice geometry (bipartite structure).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a ferrimagnetic ground state spin texture ($\mathbf{S}_A = +S e_z$, $\mathbf{S}_B = -S e_z$) and relies on the fact that ZEMs have zero weight at magnetic impurity sites.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the magnetic bipartite graph structure, the energy spectrum showing ZEMs, and the calculated magnetic couplings as a function of distance R, distinguishing between intra-sublattice (ferro) and inter-sublattice (antiferro) interactions.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the Hamiltonian and identifying the failure points of perturbative methods related to ZEMs. It then derives the non-perturbative coupling formula using MFT and Green's functions, culminating in the general proof for arbitrary bipartite graphs.
why_interesting: The development of a non-perturbative, universal framework for calculating magnetic exchange interactions in complex lattices is highly relevant for designing next-generation spintronic devices where precise control over long-range magnetic order is required.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Illustration of a magnetic bipartite graph. The green (respectively blue) symbols correspond to Bj with j = 1, .., ΛB (respectively Ai with i = 1, .., ΛA) and the dark lines to the hoppings tAB ij . The red arrows are the localized spins.

Figure 2. The spectrum of ˆH↑and ˆH↓. The ZEMs are de- picted in blue (respectively green) for those having a support on sublattice A only (respectively on B only). The ZEMs have zero weight at the sites occupied by magnetic impuri- ties. To each eigenstate of energy E↑ n in ↑sector corresponds an eigenstate of energy E↓ n = −E↑ n in the ↑sector.

Figure 3. The depleted 1/8 square lattice. The unit cell (7 orbitals/cell) is indicated by the square with dashed lines and the removed sites of the square lattice (A-type) by the filled grey circles. Small filled blue circles correspond to or- bitals of sublattice A, and the filled green squares to orbitals of sublattice B. The system contains two distinct plaquette configurations: gray squares centered on a vacancy and blue squares centered on a type-A atom. In the nearest-neighbor hopping case, the typical compact localized state (CLS) is lo- calized within the latter configuration, sustaining a non-zero quantum amplitude solely on the four B orbitals of the blue plaquette.

Figure 4. For a given set of positions of the magnetic im- purities, the energy difference (per cell), (Em −EAF )/Nc is plotted as a function of the total spin (per cell) of the mag- netic configuration ’m’. The large blue square corresponds to the fully polarized spin texture (F) and the small blue squares correspond to random configurations. The values of cA, cB, and JS are indicated in the figure.

Figure 5. Averaged Projected density of states (arbitrary unit) on impurity sites and on non magnetic sites as a func- tion of the energy for the AF spin texture. The orange dots and cyan ones correspond to different configuration of disor- der (random position of the magnetic impurities). The red (projection on non magnetic sites) and green (projection on magnetic sites) continuous lines are the average over these set of configurations.
